Research for the public good.

01Topics

Beyond one token at a time.

We study how continuous representations and parallel computation can expand the foundations of machine intelligence.

I.

Continuous language models

Build and understand models that generate language through continuous-state refinement. Study token representations, denoising architectures, noise conditioning, and scaling behavior.

MODELS
+ THEORY
II.

Parallel inference & reasoning

Refine multiple token positions together, and investigate how sampling and verification affect generation. Evaluate quality, diversity, and end-to-end latency under explicit compute budgets.

SAMPLING
+ EVALUATION
III.

Foundations & scaling

Study how data, compute, and model design shape learning and generalization, and how continuous language models can support reasoning and action.

FOUNDATIONS
+ SCALING

“Can parallel intelligence become a scalable foundation for language, reasoning, and action?”

02 / Open Source

An open library.
A shared foundation.

We are building an open library of continuous diffusion language models. Our goal is to make strong models easy to discover, use, and study through shared tools, reproducible experiments, and community collaboration.

Curate leading models

Collect and organize the best open-source continuous diffusion language models, with checkpoints, papers, and clear documentation.

Make models easy to use

Offer a unified API, one-click demos, and ready-to-run examples to load models, generate text, and compare methods.

Connect the community

Share reproducible experiments, compare results, and exchange ideas through community contributions and academic collaboration.

03Research

Ideas, put to the test.

Our latest work explores a central question: what should a Transformer for continuous language generation look like?

OCTOBER 2026PREPRINT

Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

Weijian Luo, Yujian Chen, Hao Jiang, Guang Cheng, Tianyang Hu

A systematic study of normalization, noise conditioning, gradient routing, and self-conditioning. LangDiT improves continuous language generation within LangFlow and transfers compatible components to a Plaid-style formulation.
